newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Feb 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A twin-engine jet crashed in Misamis Oriental shortly after flying Defence Secretary Renato de Villa to Mindanao on Saturday, killing its two pilots, the Air Transportation Office said. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Court of Appeals exceeded its authority in suspending the privatisation of the Metropolitan Waterworks and Sewerage System, presidential legal counsel Renato Cayetano said . (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- Defence Secretary Renato de Villa is not ruling out sabotage in the crash of a seven-seater jet about an hour after he and other officials alighted from it. (MANILA STANDARD)

- Fresh reports from the provinces are strengthening claims that a measles epidemic is already spreading, and climbing faster than the Department of Health could contain the desease - or news of it. (TODAY)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission has sent out a special audit team to look into the books of stockbrokers who had positioned heavily for the trading of speculative stocks being investigated by the commission. (MANILA STANDARD)
- The Philippine stock market underscored its reputation as a surprise performer last week with a series of record highs. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has decided to revoke the license of the Manila International Futures Exchange for failing to institute reforms in the commodity futures industry. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Philippine gross national product is forecast to expand by eight percent in the first semester of the year as prices of goods and services are expected to remain stable, according to the University of Asia and the Pacific. (MANILA CHRONICLE)
